autor: The Fifth and Sixth General Congregations · Pedro de Ribadeneira
titel: Limpieza de sangre — the decree De genere of 1593, and the conscience against it
quelle: Latin: the decrees of the Fifth General Congregation (1593–94), nn. 52–53, and of the Sixth (1608), n. 28, after the Institutum Societatis Iesu, vol. II (Florence 1893; Internet Archive Institutum2; US public domain), OCR emended against the page images. Spanish: Pedro de Ribadeneira, 'De prognatis genere Hebraeorum Societatis aditu non excludendis' (Madrid 1593), after Monumenta Ribadeneirae, vol. II (MHSI, Madrid 1923; IA patrispetriderib6402riba; published before 1930, US public domain), which prints the autograph of cod. Instit. 184, ff. 292–295v; the MHSI's sixteenth-century orthography kept, its editorial apparatus not carried. English: this site's unofficial working translations (CC0).
hinweis: The conscience line's second front, beside Spee: not an outside attack but the Society against itself. The early Society had refused the distinction of blood: Laínez, the second general, was of converso descent, as was Polanco, the founder's secretary; and Ribadeneira's memorial preserves, as eyewitness testimony, Ignatius's word that he would have counted it a special grace of God to be born of Jewish lineage — kin to Christ according to the flesh. The Fifth General Congregation decreed the exclusion anyway in 1593 — quoting Ignatius in support — and recorded in its own decree book the three intercessions raised against it; Ribadeneira answered with thirteen reasons, carried here complete; the Sixth Congregation softened the decree to five generations in 1608 and commanded silence on the matter; and the impediment stood until the 29th General Congregation removed it in 1946. Ribadeneira's covering letters to Aquaviva (1597 and 1608, in the same MHSI volume) are named, not carried. The paragraph numbering follows the decrees' own numbers and the memorial's own razones. Part of the concordance and the citation-bound dialogue; not part of the linguistic statistics, which describe the core corpus only.

sections.blurb: The Fifth General Congregation, decrees 52 and 53: the exclusion of candidates 'of Hebrew or Saracen stock', the reasons given — with Ignatius quoted for the purpose — the ruling that not even the General can dispense, and the three intercessions raised on the floor and voted down.

units.orig: Quoniam Societatis ministeria eo maiori cum fructu in communi animarum salute procuranda exercentur, quo Nostri longius absunt ab iis hominum conditionibus, quae aliis offendiculo esse possunt; ii autem, qui a progenitoribus modernis Christianis descendunt, plurimum et offendiculi et detrimenti (quemadmodum diuturna experientia compertum est) ordinarie in Societatem invehere consueverunt; ob eam causam multi efflagitarunt, ut praesentis Congregationis auctoritate statueretur: ne ullus posthac in Societatem admittatur, qui ex Hebraeorum aut Saracenorum genere descendat; et, si quispiam eorum per errorem admissus fuerit, cum primum de hoc impedimento constiterit, a Societate dimittatur. Placuit autem Congregationi universae statuere, quemadmodum praesenti suo decreto statuit: ut nullus omnino ex huiusmodi hominibus, qui ex Hebraeorum aut Saracenorum genere descendunt, deinceps in Societatem recipiatur. Quod si eorum quispiam errore aliquo admissus fuerit, cum primum de hoc impedimento constiterit, quocumque tempore ante professionem id detegatur, admonito prius Praeposito Generali, et exspectato eius responso, dimittatur. De qua re omnes ante admissionem perspicue admonendi erunt.
units.en: Since the ministries of the Society are exercised with the greater fruit in procuring the common salvation of souls, the further Ours stand from those conditions of men which can be a stumbling-block to others; and since those who descend from modern Christians have ordinarily been wont (as long experience has shown) to bring very much both of stumbling-block and of harm into the Society: for that cause many have urgently demanded that it be enacted by the authority of the present Congregation, that no one hereafter be admitted into the Society who descends from the stock of Hebrews or Saracens; and that if any of them should have been admitted by error, he be dismissed from the Society as soon as this impediment is established. And it pleased the whole Congregation to enact, as by this its present decree it does enact: that no one at all of such men as descend from the stock of Hebrews or Saracens be henceforth received into the Society. And if any of them should have been admitted by some error, as soon as this impediment is established — at whatever time before profession it be detected — he shall be dismissed, the Father General being first informed and his answer awaited. Of which matter all are to be plainly forewarned before admission.
units.label: Decree 52 · the exclusion

units.orig: Quamquam enim Societas pro communi salute omnibus omnia fieri optat, ut, quos poterit, Christo lucrifaciat; non tamen necessum est, ut suos ministros ex quovis hominum genere desumat. Quin potius ad maiorem Dei gloriam perfectioremque propositi sibi finis assecutionem convenientius est, ut eos habeat Operarios, qui omnibus aliis nationibus in toto orbe gratiores sint, et quibus in Ecclesia Dei libentius et fidentius utantur ii, quorum voluntas bene aut male in nos affecta (ut sanctae memoriae P. Ignatius ait) multum habet momenti, ut aditus ad divinum obsequium et animarum auxilium aperiatur aut praecludatur.
units.en: For although the Society desires, for the common salvation, to become all things to all men, that it may win to Christ whom it can; it is nevertheless not necessary that it take its ministers from every stock of men. Rather, for the greater glory of God and the more perfect attainment of the end it has set itself, it is more fitting that it have such Workers as are more acceptable to all other nations in the whole world, and whom those men may use more willingly and more confidently in the Church of God whose good or ill will toward us (as Father Ignatius of holy memory says) carries much weight for opening or closing the approach to the divine service and the help of souls.
units.label: Decree 52 · the reasons given
units.note: 'Ut sanctae memoriae P. Ignatius ait' — the decree invokes the founder for a policy Ribadeneira testifies he refused all his life, with tears: the founder quoted against the founder.

units.orig: Caeterum, cum circa huius decreti vim et efficaciam dubitatio exorta esset: utrum, quod eo decreto prohibetur, inter essentialia impedimenta, quae a Societate omnino excludunt, referri; an potius indispensabile tantum impedimentum decerni oporteret; tandem, post multa in utramque partem allata, Congregatio declaravit et statuit: hoc decretum non essentialis, sed indispensabilis impedimenti vim obtinere; sic scilicet, ut nullus omnino Superior, ac ne ipse quidem Praepositus Generalis in eo dispensare possit, atque ita deinceps in Societate integre inviolateque servandum esse.
units.en: For the rest, since a doubt had arisen about the force and efficacy of this decree — whether what is prohibited by it should be counted among the essential impediments, which exclude from the Society altogether, or whether it ought rather to be decreed only an indispensable impediment — at length, after much brought forward on either side, the Congregation declared and enacted: that this decree obtains the force not of an essential but of an indispensable impediment; in this sense, namely, that no Superior at all, not even the Father General himself, can dispense in it, and that it is thus henceforth to be kept in the Society whole and inviolate.
units.label: Decree 52 · not essential, but indispensable

units.orig: Cum proximum decretum in Congregatione legeretur, tres intercessiones a diversis Patribus factae fuerunt. Una quidem, ut cum iis, qui bona fide in Societatem ingressi essent, a P. Praeposito dispensari possit, quo in Societate retinerentur. Altera, ut eidem P. Praeposito dispensare integrum esset in quibusdam casibus perraris, ut, cum aliquis ex eo quidem sanguine, sed genere tamen nobilissimus in Societatem recipi petit, is admitti possit. Tertia, ut hoc impedimentum, non solum indispensabile sit, verum etiam inter essentialia impedimenta numeretur. Cui intercessioni ea ratione multi adhaeserunt, ut, si forte aliae binae obtinerent, in praedicto decreto dispensari posse, ipsorum quoque nomine intercessum esse censeretur. Verum, cum denuo de hac quaestione multa in medium a Patribus prolata fuissent, et rogata suffragia; Congregatio magna animorum ac sententiarum consensione priores duas intercessiones reiecit; et quod eo decreto ante statuit, nunc iterum decrevit, illudque ipsum decretum hoc novo decreto stabilivit, atque per omnia integre incorrupteque in Societate servandum esse, serio et graviter mandavit. Sic autem, et qui postremo loco intercesserat, a sua discessit intercessione, et ad aliorum sententiam se adiunxit.
units.en: When the foregoing decree was read in the Congregation, three intercessions were made by divers Fathers. One, that with those who had entered the Society in good faith the Father General might dispense, so that they be retained in the Society. Another, that the same Father General should be free to dispense in certain very rare cases, so that, when someone of that blood indeed, but of most noble family, asks to be received into the Society, he might be admitted. The third, that this impediment be not only indispensable, but be numbered among the essential impediments — to which intercession many adhered for this reason, that if perchance the other two should prevail and dispensation in the said decree become possible, an intercession should be considered to have been entered in their name also. But when the Fathers had again brought much into the open on this question, and the votes had been asked, the Congregation with great agreement of minds and opinions rejected the first two intercessions; and what it had before enacted by that decree it now decreed again, and established that same decree by this new decree, and seriously and gravely commanded that it be kept in the Society in all things whole and uncorrupted. And so even he who had interceded in the last place withdrew from his intercession, and joined himself to the opinion of the others.
units.label: Decree 53 · the three intercessions
units.note: Dissent recorded in the decree book itself: two intercessions sought room for dispensation and were rejected; the third wanted the bar made harsher still. The 'canon 3' that the 1608 text cites is this legislation in its canonical form.

sections.blurb: 'Las razones que se me ofrescen para no hazer nouedad en el admitir gente en la Compañía' (Madrid 1593): against the Constitutions; against the spirit of Ignatius — with the eyewitness testimony of the founder's tears; against Laínez and Borja; no true cause; against the honour of Spain; oil on the fire; against the judgment of the holiest men; the statutes themselves doubtful; and the Institute's substance at stake. On the autograph's last leaf, in Ribadeneira's hand: 'Las razones para no hazer nouedad.'

units.orig: La primera, porque es contra nuestras constituciones, las quales no excluyen a los tales, ni ponen por inpedimento essencial ni aun secundario ser de tal o tal generación.
units.en: The first: because it is against our Constitutions, which do not exclude such men, nor set it down as an essential or even a secondary impediment to be of this or that descent.
units.label: 1 · against the Constitutions

units.orig: La 2.ª, porque es derechamente contra el spíritu y sentimiento de N. P. Ignacio, el qual muchas uezes fue inportunado acerca desto del Padre Araoz, y siempre respondió que no era conforme al spíritu de Dios ni cosa que conuenía a la Compañía. Y el año de 1560, quando el Padre M.º Laínez, siendo general, embió al Padre Nadal por visitador a España, yo le di las cartas de Araoz para N. P.e sobre este punto, y las rrespuestas del Padre, para que viesse Araoz que lo quel P.e Laínez hacía en esto, era lo mismo que auía hecho antes nro. s.to Padre; y estas respuestas se hallarán en los registros de las cartas de aquel tiempo, si se buscan con atención. Item, es contra el spíritu de nro. Padre, porque yo le oy decir delante de muchos y con lágrimas en los ojos, y desde aquel tiempo lo tengo notado como cosa rara, y que nos causó admiración, que huuiera tenido por gran merced de Dios el auer nascido de judíos; y añadió la causa con estas palabras: ¡como! ¡poder ser pariente de X.º nuestro Redemptor segun la carne, y de la gloriosa Virgen María nra. Señora! Y un cauallero vizcaíno, que se llamaua Pedro de Çárate (del qual se acordarán los Padres antiguos de Roma, porque posó en nra. casa de la torre Roxa, y fue muy grande amigo de nro. Padre), me dixo que N. P. le auía dicho esto mismo, y que le auía dado tantas razones para ello, que le auía persuadido a dessearlo, con ser cosa tan contraria al natural de los vizcaínos, y que él antes tanto aborrescía. Y el Padre Euerardo, después que le elegimos general, nos contó un día sobre mesa, que Alexandro de Foligni, padre del Padre Fr. Alexandro de la orden de S.to Domingo (el qual está en Roma, y auiendo sido antes judío, se hizo christiano con su padre), en su presencia y de otros muchos que dezían que era infamia ser de linage de judíos, auía dicho: yo fuera de essa opinión, si no obstara la authoridad del Padre Ignacio, que me dixo que tuuiera por merced de Dios auer nascido deste linage.
units.en: The second: because it is directly against the spirit and mind of our Father Ignatius, who was many times importuned about this by Father Araoz, and always answered that it was not conformable to the spirit of God, nor a thing that suited the Society. And in the year 1560, when Father Master Laínez, being general, sent Father Nadal as visitor to Spain, I gave him Araoz's letters to our Father on this point, and the Father's replies, that Araoz might see that what Father Laínez was doing in this was the same that our holy Father had done before; and these replies will be found in the registers of the letters of that time, if they are searched with attention. Item, it is against the spirit of our Father, because I heard him say, before many and with tears in his eyes — and from that time I have noted it as a rare thing, and one that filled us with wonder — that he would have held it a great mercy of God to have been born of Jews; and he added the reason in these words: What! — to be able to be a kinsman of Christ our Redeemer according to the flesh, and of the glorious Virgin Mary our Lady! And a Biscayan gentleman named Pedro de Çárate (whom the old Fathers of Rome will remember, for he lodged in our house of the Torre Rossa and was a very great friend of our Father) told me that our Father had said this same thing to him, and had given him so many reasons for it that he had persuaded him to desire it — a thing so contrary to the nature of the Biscayans, and one he had before so much abhorred. And Father Everard [Mercurian], after we elected him general, told us one day at table that Alexander of Foligno, father of Father Fra Alexander of the Order of St Dominic (who is in Rome, and having before been a Jew became a Christian with his father), in his presence and that of many others who were saying it was an infamy to be of the lineage of Jews, had said: I should be of that opinion, did not the authority of Father Ignatius stand against it, who told me that he would have held it a mercy of God to have been born of this lineage.
units.label: 2 · against the spirit of Ignatius — the testimony
units.note: The module's centre: 'yo le oy decir delante de muchos y con lágrimas en los ojos … que huuiera tenido por gran merced de Dios el auer nascido de judíos' — with the corroborating witnesses Pedro de Çárate and, at Mercurian's table, Alexander of Foligno.

units.orig: La 3.ª, porque es contra el spíritu y juicio del Padre Maestro Laínez, varón tan sancto y tan sabio y tan benemérito de la Compañía, el qual, siendo general y siguiendo el spíritu de su sancto Padre Ignacio, en vna carta de diez y nueue de Nouiembre del año de 1560, escriuiendo al Padre Araoz que picaua en esto, le dize: Nunca permita nro. Señor que ni el fauor de los reyes, ni las visitas actiuas o pasiuas de grandes, ni el humor o error nacional, ni la altiuez del proprio juicio y sentimiento, ni el asco o desprecio de la agena carne, como si fuesse de otro metal la suya, o por otro Dios criada su alma que la agena, le oscuren o quiten el conoscimiento, que ha de tener un no fingido religioso, de la vnión y respecto que deue a sus superiores, aunque fuessen (como dizen) un palo; y de la circunspection en no soltar contra ellos la lengua y dar occasión a los que oyen, o de escandalizarse del poco temor de Dios del que habla, o de amotinarse dexando la vnión con su cabeça y siguiendo a quien frustra inflatur in sensu cordis sui, priuado de su cabeça y del diuino influxo, que por ella uiene. De donde nasce que uno diga: Ego sum Pauli, y murmure de Cepha, y otros al contrario; y que vno diga a lo menos con las obras: Deus est Deus tantum gentium, y otro: est Deus tantum iudaeorum, cum tamen idem sit dominus omnium, diues in omnes qui inuocant eum, modo inuocent eum in ueritate. Y por esto, los que conozen estas uerdades, creo que toman mejor camino escudándose con ellas, para uencer y burlarse de las vanas opiniones y errores y passiones contrarias del mundo, que los que por no desplacer al mundo, se configuran a él, y por placerle y yr adelante dél la cabeça descubierta, afligen los innocentes, y ciérranles de su parte los ordinarios caminos de la perfection y paz euangélica. Pero espero en nuestro S.or, muerto por todos y saluador de todos, que no preualescerá esto en su mínima Compañía, sino que por el decir del mundo no dexaremos de guardar nro. Instituto; el qual siguiendo, idem dicemus omnes, et non erunt in nobis schismata, et Dominus conteret Sathan sub pedibus nris. Y en otra carta de 23 de Nouiembre del año de 1564 responde también de su mano al mismo Padre Araoz acerca desto estas palabras: Quanto al aceptar personas con nota, por acá no se aceptan personas que tengan nota segun la ley de Dios o canónica; en las que tienen nota segun las imaginaciones, parece que basta guardarse o moderarse en las tierras donde reynan los tales humores ad duriciam cordis eorum; donde no reynan, no ay para qué impedir el bien de los que entran, y de los que son por ellos ayudados, pues in omni gente qui timet Deum, et operatur iustitiam, acceptus est Domino; y conforme a esto por acá se procede, y creo nro. S.or se sirue dello.
units.en: The third: because it is against the spirit and judgment of Father Master Laínez, a man so holy, so wise and so well-deserving of the Society, who, being general and following the spirit of his holy Father Ignatius, in a letter of the nineteenth of November of the year 1560, writing to Father Araoz, who kept pricking at this, says to him: May our Lord never permit that either the favour of kings, or the visits given and received of the great, or the national humour or error, or the haughtiness of one's own judgment and feeling, or the disgust and contempt of another's flesh — as though one's own were of other metal, or one's soul created by another God than his neighbour's — should darken or take from him the knowledge which an unfeigned religious must have of the union and respect he owes his superiors, though they were (as they say) a stick of wood; and of the circumspection not to loose his tongue against them, and give occasion to those who hear either to be scandalised at the little fear of God in the speaker, or to mutiny, leaving the union with their head and following one who is vainly puffed up in the sense of his own heart, cut off from his head and from the divine influence that comes through it. Whence it comes that one says, I am of Paul, and murmurs against Cephas, and others the contrary; and that one says, at least by his works, God is the God of the Gentiles only, and another, He is the God of the Jews only — whereas the same is Lord of all, rich unto all who call upon him, provided they call upon him in truth. And therefore those who know these truths take, I believe, the better way who shield themselves with them, to conquer and to laugh at the vain opinions and errors and contrary passions of the world, than those who, in order not to displease the world, conform themselves to it, and to please it and walk before it bare-headed, afflict the innocent and close to them, for their part, the ordinary ways of perfection and evangelical peace. But I hope in our Lord, who died for all and is the Saviour of all, that this will not prevail in his least Society, but that for the world's talk we shall not cease to keep our Institute; which following, we shall all say the same thing, and there will be no schisms among us, and the Lord will crush Satan under our feet. And in another letter, of the 23rd of November of the year 1564, he answers, likewise in his own hand, the same Father Araoz on this matter in these words: As to accepting persons with a taint: here we accept no persons who bear a taint according to the law of God or canon law; as to those who bear a taint according to the imaginations, it seems enough to be on one's guard, or to use moderation, in the lands where such humours reign, for the hardness of their hearts; where they do not reign, there is no reason to hinder the good of those who enter, and of those who are helped by them, since in every nation he that feareth God and worketh justice is accepted of the Lord; and according to this we proceed here, and I believe our Lord is served by it.
units.label: 3 · against Laínez — his letters to Araoz
units.note: Laínez — himself of converso descent — to the campaigner Araoz, 1560: 'ni el asco o desprecio de la agena carne, como si fuesse de otro metal la suya, o por otro Dios criada su alma que la agena…'

units.orig: La 4.ª, porque es contra el spíritu y uso del Padre Francisco de Borja, el qual, con ser varón illustríssimo y tan experimentado en las cosas de España, fue aún más fácil en recibir a esta gente que los Padres M.º Ignacio y M.º Laínez. Y contándome el mismo Padre un día que Ruy Gómez le auía dicho que cómo la Compañía recibía a los tales, me dixo que le auía respondido: ¿como el rey tiene en su seruicio a fulano y a fulano, que son deste linage? Pues si su Magestad no mira esso en los que admite a su seruicio, y mete en su casa; ¿queréis vos que lo mire yo para admitirlos en la casa de Dios y al seruicio de aquel Señor, apud quem non est acceptio personarum, neque distinctio iudaei et graeci, neque barbarus neque scytha?
units.en: The fourth: because it is against the spirit and practice of Father Francis Borgia, who, though a most illustrious man and deeply experienced in the affairs of Spain, was even readier to receive these people than Fathers Master Ignatius and Master Laínez. And the same Father, telling me one day that Ruy Gómez had asked him how the Society came to receive such men, told me he had answered him: How is it that the king has in his service so-and-so and so-and-so, who are of this lineage? If then his Majesty does not look at that in those he admits to his service and brings into his house, would you have me look at it in admitting them into the house of God, and to the service of that Lord with whom there is no respect of persons, nor distinction of Jew and Greek, neither barbarian nor Scythian?
units.label: 4 · against Borja — the retort to Ruy Gómez

units.orig: La 5.ª, por ser contra el uso y plática de toda la Compañía hasta aora, y contra el parescer del mismo P.e N. Claudio Aquauiua, y auerse uisto que Dios se ha seruido dello; y la Compañía ha tenido unión entre sí y lustre y buen nombre con los de fuera, y no es justo alterar las obras de Dios, y peruertir sin causa lo que sanctamente está establecido.
units.en: The fifth: because it is against the practice and usage of the whole Society until now, and against the opinion of our Father Claudio Aquaviva himself; and it has been seen that God has been served by it, and the Society has had union within itself, and lustre and good name with those without; and it is not just to alter the works of God, and to pervert without cause what is holily established.
units.label: 5 · against the Society's own practice

units.orig: La 6.ª, porque no hay causa para hazer mudança; ni la que se alega de los perturbadores es verdadera, ni bastante para hazerse. No es uerdadera, porque no se puede decir que por ser ellos de tal sangre o linage han perturbado la Compañía. Lo primero, porque otros a hauido que sauemos que han tenido mano en estos negocios, los quales son tenidos por limpios en Castilla y Portogal, como Abreo, que ha sido el capitán de todos, y N. y H. y otros; de suerte que no se puede decir con uerdad que es uicio de linage, sino de las personas; pues hombres de varios linages han concurrido en esta turbación. Lo 2.º, porque muchos que por uentura son deste linage (aunque yo no sé que lo sea ninguno), son y se han mostrado muy fieles y verdaderos hijos de nro. Padre y de la Compañía, y si el vicio estuuiera en la naturaleça, estos también siguieran a los demás. Lo 3.º, porque en tiempo de N. P.e Ignacio vbo otra borrasca, y aun más peligrosa que ésta, en Portogal, y por ella se salieron y fueron echados muchos de la Compañía, y no atribuyó nro. Padre Ignacio aquella turbación al linage, ni ellos eran tales. Y en tiempo del Padre Laínez sucedió otro alboroto bien peligroso, y se uio en gran trabajo la Compañía, y dél fueron auctores un español y dos francesses y un italiano, y entre ellos dos de los diez primeros Padres de la Compañía, y no eran deste linage. En tiempo del P.e Francisco, digo siendo comissario general, él padesció muy mucho, y se vio muy afligido y la Compañía en su persona, por ser tan principal; y el que decían que era auctor desta tribulación, no era de sangre de judíos, sino a su parescer más linpio que el sol. En tiempo del Padre Euerardo, ya sauemos los memoriales que se dieron al Papa contra él y su gouierno, y que los que los dieron, eran italianos, y lo que en esto se hizo y en lo que ha parado. Assí que, no ay que marauillarse de lo que agora se a hecho, ni que dar non causam pro causa, pues en todo tiempo a hauido trabajo, y le han dado hombres de diferentes naciones y linages. Pero aunque fuera uerdad, no era bastante causa para hazerse nouedad en esto. Lo primero, porque no es justo que por pocos ruynes padezcan muchos que no tienen culpa, ni que se tenga más cuenta con los que oppugnaron la Compañía, que con los que la defendieron, ni con los pocos que alborotaron, que con los muchos que sossegaron. La 2.ª, porque si miramos los principios, progresso, propagación y fructo de la Compañía, y las personas que nro. S.or ha tomado por instrumento para obrar lo que ha obrado, hallaremos que entre los hombres más insignes en santidad, letras, prudencia y raros dones de la Compañía, algunos a hauido deste linage, y que Dios ha mostrado que no tiene cuenta con la sangre que tomamos de nros. padres, sino con la que él derramó por nosotros en la cruz; y que, como dize el Spíritu S.to y lo trae en su carta el P. Laínez, in omni gente qui timet Deum et operatur iustitiam acceptus est illi. Y si uemos que en Italia el Padre Juan Baptista Romano, con auer sido antes judío y entrado ya hombre en la Compañía, fue sieruo de Dios y trauajó y padesció mucho por la Compañía y por la Iglesia de Dios, y que fue embiado de dos papas a Oriente, sauiendo que por sus pies se auía venido a la pila; y Fr. Alexandre en la orden de S.to Domingo oy día es tan grande predicador y de tanta autoridad, y que no le empece el auer sido antes judío y de padres judíos; ¿por qué en España se ha de tener tanta cuenta con los que uienen deste linage, estando ya purgada la culpa que tuuieron sus agüelos con el discurso de tantos años y con la bondad de sus hijos?
units.en: The sixth: because there is no cause for making a change; neither is the cause alleged — the disturbers — true, nor would it suffice if it were. It is not true, because it cannot be said that they have disturbed the Society through being of such blood or lineage. First, because there have been others who, as we know, have had a hand in these affairs, and who are held to be 'clean' in Castile and Portugal — as Abreu, who has been the captain of them all, and N. and H. and others; so that it cannot truthfully be said to be a vice of lineage, but of persons, since men of various lineages have concurred in this disturbance. Secondly, because many who perchance are of this lineage (though I do not know that any one of them is) are and have shown themselves most faithful and true sons of our Father and of the Society; and if the vice lay in the nature, these too would have followed the rest. Thirdly, because in the time of our Father Ignatius there was another storm, and a more dangerous one than this, in Portugal, and through it many left or were put out of the Society; and our Father Ignatius did not attribute that disturbance to lineage, nor were they of it. And in the time of Father Laínez there occurred another most dangerous tumult, and the Society found itself in great travail; and its authors were a Spaniard, two Frenchmen and an Italian, among them two of the first ten Fathers of the Society — and they were not of this lineage. In the time of Father Francis, I mean while he was commissary general, he suffered very much, and was sorely afflicted, and the Society in his person, he being so eminent; and the man they said was the author of that tribulation was not of the blood of Jews, but in his own conceit cleaner than the sun. In the time of Father Everard we all know the memorials that were given to the Pope against him and his government, and that those who gave them were Italians, and what was done in the matter and how it ended. So there is no cause to marvel at what has now been done, nor to give what is no cause for the cause, since in every age there has been trouble, and men of different nations and lineages have given it. But even were it true, it would not be cause enough to make an innovation in this. First, because it is not just that for a few wretches many should suffer who bear no guilt, nor that more account be taken of those who fought against the Society than of those who defended it, nor of the few who raised tumults than of the many who stilled them. Secondly, because if we look at the beginnings, progress, propagation and fruit of the Society, and at the persons our Lord has taken as instruments to work what he has worked, we shall find that among the men most distinguished in the Society for sanctity, learning, prudence and rare gifts, there have been some of this lineage; and that God has shown that he takes no account of the blood we receive from our fathers, but of that which he shed for us on the cross; and that, as the Holy Spirit says, and Father Laínez carries it in his letter, in every nation he that feareth God and worketh justice is accepted of him. And if we see that in Italy Father Giovanni Battista Romano, though he had before been a Jew and entered the Society already a grown man, was a servant of God and laboured and suffered much for the Society and for the Church of God, and was sent by two popes to the East, though it was known that he had come to the font on his own feet; and that Fra Alexander in the Order of St Dominic is at this day so great a preacher and of such authority, and it hinders him not to have before been a Jew and of Jewish parents — why in Spain must so much account be taken of those who come of this lineage, the fault of their grandfathers being now purged by the course of so many years and by the goodness of their sons?
units.label: 6 · the alleged cause is neither true nor sufficient
units.note: The empirical argument: every disturbance in the Society's history, sorted by actual authors — 'no se puede decir con uerdad que es uicio de linage, sino de las personas.'

units.orig: De aquí se sigue la 7.ª razón, que esto es contra la honrra de la Compañía de España y aun de toda la nación española: la qual, o se ha de tener toda por judía y marrana, como la llaman en Italia, o por tonta y loca; por judía, si ay causa para hacer estatutos y diferencias de linajes, pues en ninguna otra nación, aun entre los que oy biuen judíos y tienen sus sinagogas, ay esta diferencia; y sabemos que aun en el collegio de los cardenales a hauido en nros. días personas que descienden deste linage, a los quales en algunas yglesias de España no dieran una capellanía, con auer ya cien años que no ay judíos en los reynos de Castilla; por loca y desbaratada, si sin necessidad se deshonrra y afrenta.
units.en: From this follows the seventh reason: that this is against the honour of the Society of Spain, and indeed of the whole Spanish nation; which must either be held all Jewish and marrana, as they call it in Italy, or foolish and mad. Jewish, if there is cause for making statutes and distinctions of lineages — since in no other nation, even among those who today live as Jews and have their synagogues, does this distinction exist; and we know that even in the college of cardinals there have been in our days persons who descend from this lineage, to whom in some churches of Spain they would not give a chaplaincy, though it is now a hundred years since there have been Jews in the realms of Castile. And foolish and reckless, if without necessity she dishonours and affronts herself.
units.label: 7 · against the honour of Spain

units.orig: La 8.ª: si pretendemos vnir la Compañía y soldar nras. quiebras y apagar este incendio que el demonio ha leuantado, ¿pensamos que será buen medio el desunirla y despedaçarla más, y hazer que no aya hermano que mire con buenos ojos a su hermano, sino como a enemigo y como a hombre de otra casta y secta, y echar azeite en el fuego para que se encienda más y abrase y consuma a toda la Compañía? ¿Qué seso sería éste? ¿qué pecado? ¿qué ofensa de Dios y qué daño tan perjudicial e irreparable? Y si el P.e general agora tiene algunos Padres quexosos por la sequedad con que les parece que su Paternidad los ha tratado, ¿quánto más serían los que se tentarían y afligirían y por uentura se harían de hijos fieles enemigos crueles? Otra uez, de sólo imaginarse que un Padre tenía este humor y trataua desta materia, huuo en España grande alboroto y desassosiego, y no se aplacó hasta que el mismo P.e desengañó a los que esto pensauan, mostrando que no pretendía nouedad, ni le parescía bien que la huuiesse azerca desto en la Compañía.
units.en: The eighth: if we mean to unite the Society, and solder our fractures, and put out this fire the demon has kindled, do we think it a good means to disunite and dismember her further, and to bring it about that no brother looks on his brother with good eyes, but as on an enemy and a man of another caste and sect — to pour oil on the fire, that it may blaze the higher and scorch and consume the whole Society? What sense would this be? what sin? what offence against God, and what harm, so prejudicial and irreparable? And if the Father General now has some Fathers aggrieved at the dryness with which they think his Paternity has treated them, how many more would be tempted and afflicted, and perchance turn from faithful sons into cruel enemies? Once before, at the mere imagination that one Father was of this humour and was dealing in this matter, there was great tumult and disquiet in Spain, and it was not stilled until that same Father undeceived those who thought it, showing that he intended no innovation, nor thought it good that there should be any in the Society concerning this.
units.label: 8 · oil on the fire

units.orig: La 9.ª: esto es contra el parescer de los hombres más santos, más religiosos, más graues y amigos de la Compañía. Más santos, porque el P.e Maestro Áuila dixo que por dos cosas se podría perder la Compañía: la primera, por admitir a ella mucha turba; y la 2.ª, por hacer distinción de linages y sangre. Más religiosos, porque los que lo son más, y más amigos de la Compañía, alaban sumamente lo que ella haze, y dicen claramente que en haciendo estatuto, se perderá, porque entrará el fuego de la discordia en ella, la diuisión y guerra doméstica y entrañable, como la ay en las otras religiones que tienen estatuto. Los más graues y amigos, porque a mí mismo me lo han dicho, dándoles yo razón de lo que ordenan nras. Constituciones y usa la Compañía, diziéndome que aunque para los oficios de inquisición sea necessario, y para los otros consejos, collegios y yglesias seculares esto se pueda por uentura en alguna manera tolerar, pero que para las religiones, que professan menosprecio del mundo y perfecta imitación de X.º, les parece muy mal; y que, si Sto. Thomás no quiere que el recién conuertido piense mucho si entrará en religión, quando Dios le llama, mucho menos la religión ha de echar al que llama Dios, por nascer de agüelos o de uisagüelos, que aora ciento o ducientos años se conuirtieron. Y hablando yo con el señor cardenal de Toledo e inquisidor general, y dándole las razones que tiene la Compañía para dessear que el sancto Officio no la ocupe en el officio de consultores, aunque siempre esté aparejada para obedescer, le dixe que agora biuíamos en paz, y que auiendo consultores, podría ser que se turbasse; porque, como los que lo han de ser, han de tener cierta calidad de sangre y limpieza, si se echase mano de algunos que la tienen y no tantas letras y prudencia, dexando a los que son auentajados en esto, por no ser tan limpios, auría nota y causaría diuissión; me dixo que tenía razón. Y otras personas graues lo han aprouado, por lo que nos inporta el ser todos cor unum et anima una; y aun porque un cauallero, nro. amigo, auía dicho al cardenal de Toledo que un judío entre otros era el que turbaua la Compañía, pensando el cardenal que este dicho nascía de la Compañía, me le afeó mucho y me dixo: ¿Es éste lenguage de la Compañía?
units.en: The ninth: this is against the opinion of the men most holy, most religious, most grave, and most friendly to the Society. Most holy: for Father Master Ávila said that by two things the Society could be lost — the first, by admitting into her a great crowd; and the second, by making distinction of lineages and blood. Most religious: for those who are most so, and most friends of the Society, praise supremely what she does, and say plainly that in making a statute she will be lost, for the fire of discord will enter into her, division and domestic, inward war — as there is in the other religious orders that have a statute. The most grave and friendly: because they have said it to me myself, when I gave them account of what our Constitutions ordain and the Society practises, telling me that though for the offices of the Inquisition it may be necessary, and for the other councils, colleges and secular churches it may perchance in some manner be tolerated, yet for the religious orders, which profess contempt of the world and the perfect imitation of Christ, it seems to them very ill; and that, if St Thomas will not have the newly-converted deliberate long whether he shall enter religion when God calls him, much less ought religion to cast out him whom God calls, because he is born of grandfathers or great-grandfathers who were converted a hundred or two hundred years ago. And speaking myself with the lord cardinal of Toledo, the inquisitor general, and giving him the reasons the Society has for desiring that the Holy Office not employ her in the office of consultors — though she stand always ready to obey — I told him that we now lived in peace, and that were there consultors it might be disturbed; because, since those who are to hold that office must have a certain quality of blood and cleanness, if some were taken who have it, but not so much learning and prudence, passing over those who excel in these but are not so 'clean', there would be a mark, and it would cause division; and he told me I was right. And other grave persons have approved it, for how much it imports us that we be all one heart and one soul; and further, because a gentleman, a friend of ours, had said to the cardinal of Toledo that a Jew, among others, was disturbing the Society, the cardinal, thinking this saying came from within the Society, reproached me with it sharply and said to me: Is this the language of the Society?
units.label: 9 · the judgment of the holiest — Ávila's two dangers
units.note: Juan de Ávila's warning that the Society could be lost by two things only — admitting a crowd, and distinguishing lineages — and the cardinal of Toledo's rebuke: '¿Es éste lenguage de la Compañía?'

units.orig: La 10: muchos dudan si estos estatutos, como se usan, son lícitos; otros, si son expedientes; otros dizen que se cometen graues peccados; otros, que son gran tentación de uenganças, ambiçiones e inuidias y agrauios entre los religiosos, y un fuego que los abrasa y consume, y que por esto algunas religiones, que los auían inpetrado de la Sede Apostólica, se han arrepentido y les han echo rreuocar, o que no los guardan. Pues, ¿para qué la Compañía se ha de poner en estos labyrintos y dificultades? De las quales no podrá salir sin daño y escándalo de muchos, y pérdida de su authoridad y buena opinión, con la qual agora edifica y pacifica y reprehende lo que conuiene en este negocio, quando y como es menester.
units.en: The tenth: many doubt whether these statutes, as they are used, are licit; others, whether they are expedient; others say that grave sins are committed by them; others, that they are a great temptation to revenges, ambitions, envies and injuries among religious, and a fire that scorches and consumes them; and that for this reason some orders which had obtained them from the Apostolic See have repented, and had them revoked, or do not keep them. Why then should the Society put herself into these labyrinths and difficulties? — out of which she will not come without harm and scandal to many, and the loss of her authority and good repute, with which she now edifies and pacifies, and rebukes what needs rebuking in this business, when and as is needful.
units.label: 10 · the statutes themselves are doubted

units.orig: 11. Auiendo hasta aora N. P. general seguido en esto el spíritu de los otros generales sus antecessores, si agora se mudase, ¿qué parecería al mundo, sino que es uengança, y que la desobediencia o mal término de vno le ha uencido y irritado de manera que le ha hecho mudar parecer, y que no ha tenido virtud para resistir a tan duro golpe? Por lo qual quedaría menoscabada su authoridad y la opinión, que todos con tanta razón de la persona de su Paternidad tenemos y deuemos tener.
units.en: The eleventh: our Father General having until now followed in this the spirit of the other generals his predecessors, if he were now to change, what would it seem to the world but that it is revenge — that the disobedience or ill conduct of one man has so conquered and provoked him as to make him change his mind, and that he has not had the virtue to withstand so hard a blow? Whereby his authority would be diminished, and the opinion which we all, with such good reason, hold and ought to hold of the person of his Paternity.
units.label: 11 · what the world would conclude

units.orig: 12. La muerte del Padre Alonso Sánchez en tal occasión y tiempo, ha dado mucho que pensar y que dezir; y los que más saben de sus cosas, dizen que ha sido del cielo y en gran beneficio de la Compañía, por el mal spíritu que tenía en esto; y aun añaden que ha sido castigo de Dios, por auer hablado desta materia en las informaciones que se dieron en la congregación prouincial, más de lo que conuenía, y que entonces se sembró vna zizaña y mala semilla, que para que no crezca y se arraygue, no ay otro mejor remedio sino enterrarla con perpetuo silencio y oluido. Dexo otras razones, que cada hombre cuerdo y prudente por sí mismo las podrá entender, aunque yo no las diga.
units.en: The twelfth: the death of Father Alonso Sánchez at such an occasion and time has given much to think and much to say; and those who know most of his affairs say that it was from heaven, and to the great benefit of the Society, because of the ill spirit he had in this; and they add too that it was a chastisement of God, for having spoken of this matter, in the informations given at the provincial congregation, more than was fitting; and that a cockle and evil seed was then sown, for which, that it may not grow and take root, there is no better remedy than to bury it in perpetual silence and oblivion. I leave other reasons, which every sober and prudent man will be able to understand for himself, though I do not say them.
units.label: 12 · the death of Alonso Sánchez
units.note: Alonso Sánchez, the decree's most vehement promoter, died in Madrid on 27 May 1593, weeks before the Congregation met; Ribadeneira's grim providentialism here is part of the document, carried as it stands.

units.orig: 13. Pero entre ellas es una y no de pequeña consideración, que si se mellasse y se desportillasse una uez nro. Instituto en cosa tan sustancial y de tanta inportancia, y se hiziesse decreto tan contrario al spíritu de nros. sanctos Padres Ignacio, Laínez y Francisco, y contra el uso de la Compañía, con el qual por la misericordia de Dios ella ha tanto florescido; queda abierta la puerta para enflaquecer y tocar todas las demás cosas sustanciales del mismo Instituto; porque es cierto que no ay ninguna (exceptuando las que son essenciales y contra nros. votos) que sea tan sustancial como ésta; porque ésta toca a la paz, a la unión, a la charidad, que es la uida y el alma de la religión y el fin y blanco della; y el dilatarse las professiones, el poder despedir, el ser general perpetuo o ad tempus, el hazer los superiores por su mano y no por eleción de los súbditos, y otras cosas semejantes, son medios que se toman para conseguir mejor este fin; y assí tanto más cuydado se deue poner en guardarle y defenderle que en las otras cosas que no son tan sustanciales, quanto importa más el fin que los medios.
units.en: The thirteenth: but among them is one of no small consideration — that if our Institute were once notched and breached in a thing so substantial and of such importance, and a decree were made so contrary to the spirit of our holy Fathers Ignatius, Laínez and Francis, and against the usage of the Society, with which by the mercy of God she has so greatly flourished, the door stands open to weaken and to touch all the other substantial things of the same Institute. For it is certain that there is none (excepting those that are essential and against our vows) so substantial as this; because this touches the peace, the union, the charity, which is the life and the soul of the religious order and its end and mark; and the deferring of professions, the power to dismiss, the general's office perpetual or for a term, the making of superiors by his hand and not by election of the subjects, and other like things, are means taken the better to attain this end; and so the more care must be put into keeping and defending it than into the other things that are not so substantial, by as much as the end imports more than the means.
units.label: 13 · the Institute's substance at stake
units.note: On the autograph's last leaf, in Ribadeneira's hand: 'Las razones para no hazer nouedad.' A later hand added, and another — rightly, say the MHSI editors — struck out: 'Che non si deue mutare il decreto de genere.'

sections.titel: The mitigation of 1608 — five generations, and silence
sections.blurb: The Sixth General Congregation, decree 28: after three sessions, the inquiry limited to five generations, proof required instead of rumour — and, at the close, a commanded silence 'for the keeping of charity and union among Ours'. The impediment itself stood until 1946.

units.orig: Propositum fuerat Congregationi: ut informatio, quae fieri debet ad servandum canonem tertium Congregationis quintae generalis, illa censeretur sufficiens, in qua testes deponerent de quatuor vel quinque generationibus: in hac vero non haberetur ratio de rumoribus, sed probationes sint certo concludentes, aliquam personam in particulari fuisse ad fidem conversam ex Iudaismo vel Mahumetismo. Cum igitur Congregatio hac de re diligenter et hinc inde allatis rationibus per tres sessiones egisset; tandem decrevit per modum, sive declarationis, sive moderationis: eam in posterum praxim esse adhibendam, ut, exclusis iis, qui Morisci in Hispania vocantur, vel aliis quibuscumque, qui christiani quasi specie tenus haberentur, de his enim non agitur; itemque iis, qui hoc nomine generationis Hebraeorum seu Saracenorum infames habentur, qui etiam iuxta Constitutiones titulo infamiae admitti non possunt; in caeteris, qui alioqui honestae familiae essent, aut vulgo nobiles, vel boni nominis haberentur, informationes fierent usque ad quintum gradum inclusive. In quibus informationibus, quae diligenter, secreto et prudenter faciendae erunt, exacte tamen, sicuti non est habenda ratio cuiuscumque rumoris, aut cuiuspiam asserentis se aliquid inaudisse; ita, si constans fama haberetur, tales hac macula notatos, unde offendiculo et dedecori esse possent, non essent admittendi; sed probationes certae et fide dignae habendae erunt, ut aliquis usque ad eum gradum excludatur. Ultra hos vero gradus, nisi sit talis infamia, quae publice constet, decrevit Congregatio: non esse, aut censendum impedimentum aliquod, aut ulterius inquirendum. De Tartaris autem et Mahumetanis aliis, sive in Polonia, sive alibi, committitur R. P. N. Generali, ut possit dispensare intra praedictos hos gradus, cum cesset in his ratio infamiae et dedecoris.
units.en: It had been proposed to the Congregation that the information which must be made to keep the third canon of the Fifth General Congregation be judged sufficient when the witnesses deposed concerning four or five generations; and that in it no account be taken of rumours, but the proofs be certainly conclusive that some particular person had been converted to the faith from Judaism or Mohammedanism. When therefore the Congregation had dealt diligently with this matter, reasons being brought on either side, through three sessions, it at length decreed, by way whether of declaration or of moderation: that hereafter this practice be used — that (setting aside those who in Spain are called Moriscos, or any others who would be held Christians as it were in appearance only, for of these there is no question; and likewise those who are held infamous under this name of the stock of Hebrews or Saracens, who even according to the Constitutions cannot be admitted under the title of infamy) in the case of the rest, who are otherwise of honourable family, or commonly held noble or of good name, the informations be made up to the fifth degree inclusive. In which informations — to be made diligently, secretly and prudently, yet exactly — just as no account is to be taken of any rumour, or of anyone asserting that he has heard something; so, if there were a constant report that such men were marked with this stain, whence they might be a stumbling-block and a disgrace, they would not be admitted; but the proofs must be certain and worthy of credit, for anyone to be excluded up to that degree. Beyond these degrees, unless there be such infamy as is publicly established, the Congregation decreed that there is no impediment to be reckoned, nor any further inquiry to be made. As for Tartars and other Mohammedans, whether in Poland or elsewhere, it is committed to our Reverend Father General to be able to dispense within the aforesaid degrees, when in them the reason of infamy and disgrace ceases.
units.label: Decree 28 · five generations, proof not rumour

units.orig: Atque hac occasione ad charitatem et unionem inter Nostros servandam, ne quis incertis rumoribus detur locus, aut spargantur inter Nostros quae etiam Superiores et alios praestantes Operarios laedere et contemptibiles reddere possunt, commendat serio et diligenter Congregatio omnibus Nostris: ne de huiusmodi rebus sermones misceantur; monitis tamen, ubi opus fuerit, Superioribus, si quid irrepserit, quod contra hoc decretum seu moderationem esse possit, ut illi pro suo officio remedium adhibeant, vel R. P. N. Generalem admoneant.
units.en: And on this occasion, for the keeping of charity and union among Ours — lest any place be given to uncertain rumours, or things be spread among Ours which can wound even Superiors and other excellent Workers and render them contemptible — the Congregation seriously and diligently commends to all Ours: that no talk be mingled of matters of this kind; the Superiors being nevertheless informed, where need shall be, if anything creep in that could be against this decree or moderation, that they may apply the remedy according to their office, or advise our Reverend Father General.
units.label: Decree 28 · the commanded silence
units.note: The wound managed, not healed: the same decree that narrows the inquiry forbids Ours to speak of such matters. The 29th General Congregation abrogated the impediment of origin in 1946 (decree 8) — three and a half centuries after Ribadeneira asked for its burial 'con perpetuo silencio y oluido', though not the silence he meant.
